thread:
maria: heads-up: after the 02:00 deploy of model-x v2026-03-tokenizer we’re seeing p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~730ms for gen endpoints in us-west-2. impact across ~15% of requests. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployment completed: model-x@v2026-03-tokenizer -> prod by sam at 2026-03-17T02:00:12Z

sam: thanks, looking. did we change tokenizer or model weights in this rollout?

maria: tokenizer + small token-normalization tweak (split punctuation differently). also seq-len distribution looks shifted right. quick numbers from logs: old median tokens=38, new median tokens=62, p99 old=240 new=420.

alex: can you paste a repro tokenization diff? noisy neighbor question: are the affected pods colocated with other noisy workloads?

maria: sample diff:
```
old: "Deploy the agent to the prod cluster." -> [Deploy, the, agent, to, the, prod, cluster, .] (8 tokens)
new: "Deploy the agent to the prod cluster." -> [Deploy, the, agent, to, the, prod, cluster, ., "\u0120"] (12 tokens, some tokens split differently)
```

sam: confirmed the tokenizer graph change. that will increase decoded length and KV cache sizes. I also noticed kernel selection logs on canaries: `kernel_policy=auto -> fallback=attention_simple` on several hot shards.

jeff: checked runtime logs, here's a condensed snippet from the node that hit worst p95:
```
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] model_x shard-12 kernel_select: chosen_kernel=attention_fast, fallback=attention_simple, kernel_fallback=1
[2026-03-17T02:15:03Z] batching: batch_size=4, target_latency_ms=150, observed_latency_ms=420
[2026-03-17T02:15:04Z] kvcache: miss_rate=0.27, avg_kv_size=1.9MB
[2026-03-17T02:15:05Z] gpu_mem: utilization=78%, free=3.2GB
```

alex: kernel_fallback=1 is the smoking gun. attention_fast/regression usually triggered by changed sequence lengths or an input shape not compiled into fast path, so runtime falls back to simpler (slower) kernel. combined with bigger seq-len -> batching heuristics fragment batches -> more tiny batches -> higher per-token overhead. also saw intermittent memcpy spikes in profiler.

maria: attached a short flame from the profiler run on the pod (summarized):
```
45% time -> attention_simple (FP32)
20% time -> cudaMemcpyAsync (KV spill / restore)
10% time -> tokenizer postproc
8% time -> allocator (fragmentation)
7% time -> batching/queue wait
```

sam: tokenizer change increased avg token count by ~1.6x on our prompt set. that multiplies kvcache memory working set and pushes some shards over quantization/packing thresholds we use to pick kernels. i think kernel selection rule used sequence-length buckets; new tokenization pushed some requests into a bucket that lacks optimized kernels.

jeff: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back tokenizer change (fastest), 2) force kernel pinning to `attention_fast` for the model (risky), 3) adjust batching window to increase microbatching tolerance, 4) enable KV cache warmup to reduce memcpy spikes.

alex: for short-term I'd prefer rollback to previous model & tokenizer, and then do a gradual canary with perf checks. we should also add a runtime metric: `kernel_fallback_rate` per-model-per-shard and an alert at >1% sustained.

maria: rolling back now to model-x@v2026-02-tokenizer, canary 100% -> back to stable by 02:22 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: model-x@v2026-02-tokenizer restored to prod by maria at 2026-03-17T02:22:09Z

sam: great. follow-ups: (a) add a tokenizer integration perf test that validates seq-len distribution against a golden prompt set before rollout, (b) add automatic kernel-selection simulation in CI (run a fast compile + select step for representative seq-lens), (c) avoid tokenizer changes that materially increase token counts without perf signoff.

jeff: created infra ticket INF-2217 to expose kernel_fallback_rate and kvcopy latencies in console. tagged eng-runtime + eng-ml.

alex: creating incident note and postmortem stub. initial RCA: tokenizer change -> increased seq-len -> changed kernel selection bucket -> fallback to slower kernel + increased KV cache memcpy -> batching fragmentation -> p95 spike. mitigation: rollback + add observability.

maria: quick note for oncall playbook: when p95 doubles after model rollout check: tokenization diffs, kernel_fallback_rate, kvcache miss rate, batch_size histogram.

sam: i'll push the tokenizer revert PR to main branch and add perf-test hooks. also we'll run a 1% canary with kernel_fallback monitoring before next rollout.

maria: thanks everyone. we should schedule a follow-up in eng-runtime sync tomorrow to walk through perf tuning (kernel policies, batching heuristics, KV warmup). :thumbsup:

alex: assigning postmortem ownership to sam. closing slack thread. :white_check_mark:
